findings.topic: Update process requires manual git surgery
findings.message: The success criteria explicitly promises 'no manual git surgery', yet Phase 4 contradicts this by requiring the operator to manually execute `git stash`, run the update, perform `git stash pop`, and resolve any resulting merge conflicts themselves if they have local edits. This violates the premise of a low-friction package that a collaborator can easily run and maintain.

findings.topic: Archive hash verification impossible with git distribution
findings.message: The first-contact integrity ceremony instructs the operator to 'verify the archive hash against the out-of-band value.' However, Phase 4 dictates distribution via a persistent git release branch. Because the operator is cloning a repository rather than downloading a monolithic release tarball, there is no 'archive' to hash. This makes the critical initial trust anchor technically impossible for the operator to execute.

findings.topic: 90-second headless pairing timeout is operationally hostile
findings.message: The one-time pairing code for headless environments expires in 90 seconds. In a real-world operator scenario involving remote servers, establishing an SSH tunnel, switching machine contexts, opening a browser, and typing the code can easily exceed this limit, leading to frustrating timeouts during onboarding.
